# Preface {.unnumbered}

This report presents our group project for **IFN646 Biomedical Data Science
at Queensland University of Technology**. It connects three stages of a
biomedical data analysis: identifying changes in gene expression, selecting
CRISPR guide RNAs, and assessing how human genetic variation may affect
those guides.

The project uses real biomedical data within a teaching scenario. Its
working hypothesis is that regulating genes affected by COVID-19 could
support recovery. This hypothesis provides a reason for the analysis;
the project does not test whether the proposed guides improve clinical
outcomes.

The report follows the decisions from the RNA-seq analysis to the evaluation
of **OAS2** and the selected guides **200forw** and **248forw**. Each task
explains the approach, presents the findings, and discusses what the
results support. The final chapters bring these findings together and
document how to reproduce the analysis.

## How to read this report

| Chapter | Purpose |
|:--|:--|
| [Introduction](intro.qmd) | Explain the project context and the questions addressed. |
| [Task 1](Task1.qmd) | Analyse differential expression and combine evidence from the selected tools. |
| [Task 2](Task2.qmd) | Explain the choice of OAS2 and assess guide efficiency and specificity. |
| [Task 3](Task3.qmd) | Reassess the guides using individual variant information. |
| [Summary](summary.qmd) | Connect the findings and explain the main limitations. |
| [Reproducibility](reproducibility.qmd) | Describe the required files and how to run the analysis. |
| [References](references.qmd) | List the sources cited throughout the report. |

Analysis code is available in expandable blocks. Important tables and
figures remain visible so that the main findings can be read without
opening the code.
